title: Spot Assay and Colony Forming Unit (CFU) Analyses for Candida and Saccharomyces
author: Satya Ranjan Sahu

The same dilution will be performed for the rest of the strains (see Note 3). Critical: Before pipetting out 20 μL, mix it evenly for uniform cell density and efficient serial dilution. Spotting of dilutions Sterilize the spotter by dipping the pins in 100% ethanol kept in a glass Petri dish, followed by brief flaming three times. Allow the spotter to cool down (5–10 min) (see Note 4). Caution: Keep the spirit lamp or Bunsen burner away from the vertical airflow well inside the laminar hood. Placing the lamp too close to the airflow may cause over-flaming due to the introduction of air, which could potentially lead to an explosion of the laminar hood. Place the spirit lamp and the Petri dish with 100% ethanol in two separate corners of the laminar hood. Immediately close the lid of the spirit lamp after flaming. Once the spotter cools down completely, dip the spotter into the 96-well plate with the serial dilutions of cultures and spot gently on the agar plates with or without cytotoxic agents. Take out the spotter vertically without disturbing the plate (see Note 5). Spotting has to be done separately for each plate. After spotting, leave the plates undisturbed for 10–15 min to ensure complete absorption of spotted culture; keep the plates at 30 °C for 24–48 h depending upon the growth on the plates. Critical: If the additive reagent is light-sensitive, perform spotting by switching off the laminar hood light and cover with aluminum foil during incubation. After 24 h, monitor plates at regular intervals to avoid overgrowing of spots. Spreading of dilutions for estimating CFU Pipette out 100 μL of 10 -4 diluted samples from the fifth-row wells (E1–E12), transfer into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube, and make up the volume to 600 μL with YPD broth. Critical: Depending upon the number of plates required to spread, select the dilution accordingly from the 96-well plates (10 -3 or 10 -4 ) for further dilution in 1 mL microcentrifuge tubes. If the number of plates is > 6, one can select a lower dilution and continue. Thoroughly mix the culture in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube by pipetting with a 1 mL pipette or by vortexing for a few seconds. Spread 100 μL of the resultant samples on the plates with or without reagents. Three plates containing the same concentration of HU and one YPD agar control plate will be used for spreading to get statistical significance. Incubate all plates at 30 °C for 24–48 h depending upon the growth of isolated colonies on the plates (see Additional note 2). Critical: Too few or too many colonies on the plates may give a false estimation; therefore, the dilution has to be selected in such a way that approximately 50–80 isolated colonies will appear on a plate. Pause point: Prior to imaging/counting of colonies, one can keep the plates at 4 °C by wrapping them in parafilm and aluminum foil (Figure S1). Place the plate on a light box and count the colonies manually. Note down the information with respect to each plate immediately (Additional note 3). Plates imaging Place the YPD plate from both spot and CFU analyses in an upright position on a white plate of Bio-Rad gel doc and remove the plate cover to prevent reflection. Open the Image lab software, select the stain-free blot in the blot section, and acquire the image. For best imaging, place two plates at a time (see Note 6). Export the 600 dpi image in .tif format and the raw image file in .scn format. Using any generic software (e.g., PowerPoint), arrange the spotted plates in increasing concentration order with the control plate and compare the sensitivity.

steps.title: Prepare sterile workspace
steps.instruction: Wipe the laminar flow hood with 70 % ethanol, place all required items (Petri dishes, 96‑well plates, spirit lamp, spotter, pipette set, sterile tip box, 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes) inside, turn on the UV lamp for 30 min, and wear lab coat and gloves.

steps.title: Streak yeast from glycerol stock
steps.instruction: Streak each yeast strain of interest from its glycerol stock onto a sterile YPDA agar plate and incubate for 48 h at 30 °C.

steps.title: Inoculate overnight culture
steps.instruction: Pick a single colony of each strain and inoculate into 5 mL autoclaved YPD broth; grow overnight (14–16 h) at 30 °C with shaking at 200 rpm.

steps.title: Prepare YPD agar plates
steps.instruction: Swirl freshly autoclaved YPD agar until cool enough to handle, then pour ~25 mL per plate. For drug plates, add the required volume of stock solution (e.g., 100 mM HU or 99 % MMS) to achieve final concentrations of 5, 10, 20 mM HU and 0.001, 0.002, 0.003 % MMS, mix, and pour. Pour four plates per concentration (one for spotting, three for spreading). Allow plates to cool 45–60 min, then cover and store inverted. Follow each toxic reagent’s safety sheet; for light‑sensitive reagents turn off hood light and cover plates with aluminum foil while pouring. Label plates with concentration and arrow marks indicating strain/dilution direction.

steps.title: Store plates (optional pause)
steps.instruction: Wrap plates with parafilm and aluminum foil and keep at 4 °C if spotting/spreading will be performed the next day. Long‑term storage is not recommended.

steps.title: Set up serial dilutions
steps.instruction: Dilute each overnight culture 1:10 with YPD broth in a 1.5 mL tube, measure OD600 and adjust to ~1.0 (dilute further if OD > 3). Add 200 µL of the 1.0 OD culture to the first row (S1–S12) of a round‑bottom 96‑well plate. Fill the five downstream wells in each column (B1–F1) with 180 µL YPD broth. Perform a 10‑fold serial dilution by transferring 20 µL from well to well up to well F1, yielding a 10⁻⁵ dilution (6 × 10⁶ cells → 60 cells). Repeat for each strain.

steps.title: Sterilize spotter
steps.instruction: Dip the spotter pins in 100 % ethanol placed in a glass Petri dish, then flame the pins three times over a spirit lamp. Allow the spotter to cool for 5–10 min. Keep the spirit lamp away from the vertical airflow of the hood and close the lamp lid after flaming.

steps.title: Spot dilutions onto agar
steps.instruction: After the spotter has cooled, dip it into each well of the 96‑well plate and gently spot onto the appropriate YPD agar plate (with or without drug). Perform spotting separately for each plate. After spotting, let plates sit undisturbed for 10–15 min to allow absorption. If the drug is light‑sensitive, turn off the hood light and cover plates with foil during incubation.

steps.title: Incubate spotted plates
steps.instruction: Incubate the spotted plates at 30 °C for 24–48 h (monitor after 24 h to avoid overgrowth).

steps.title: Prepare diluted samples for CFU spreading
steps.instruction: From the fifth row wells (E1–E12) of each 96‑well plate, pipette 100 µL of the 10⁻⁴ diluted culture into a 1.5 mL tube and bring the volume to 600 µL with YPD broth. Mix thoroughly by pipetting or vortexing for a few seconds.

steps.title: Spread dilutions on agar
steps.instruction: Spread 100 µL of each mixed sample onto YPD agar plates (one control plate and three plates per drug concentration). Use the appropriate dilution (10⁻³ or 10⁻⁴) depending on the number of plates; for >6 plates select a lower dilution and continue. Aim for ~50–80 isolated colonies per plate. Incubate at 30 °C for 24–48 h.

steps.title: Store plates before counting (optional pause)
steps.instruction: If colony counting will be delayed, wrap plates with parafilm and aluminum foil and keep at 4 °C.

steps.title: Image and count colonies
steps.instruction: Place each YPD plate (spot and CFU) upright on the white platform of a Bio‑Rad Gel‑Doc, remove the lid to avoid reflection, and acquire images using Image Lab (select “stain‑free blot”). Capture two plates at a time, export images at 600 dpi in .tif format and also save the raw .scn file. Arrange the images in order of increasing drug concentration (including control) and manually count colonies on the light box.
